verdict: 13 mapped-content gaps; no wholly absent recommendation or newly identified contradiction
method: Manually read when/action/because/caveats for each of the 228 A, 211 B and 223 C practices and compare their meaningful decisions, applicability and qualifications with the content of the mapped canonical practices. Content rationales are reviewer-authored semantic summaries, not automatically inferred from IDs, copied raw provenance, or candidate sentence selections. Individual candidate sentence links are not adjudicated by this review.
qualification_policy: A narrower/missing meaningful qualification is a finding even when the full inventory retains it elsewhere. F5 can be resolved by explicitly making BP197 inherited guidance for optimization records instead of duplicating wording. Explanatory examples and repeated non-operational background need not survive verbatim if the decision and its limits survive.

scope_limits: Exhaustive comparison is at the 662 raw-practice level. It does not certify every one of the 2858 automatic candidate sentence references.
The full 240-practice canonical inventory was read in the initial review and relevant corrected or disputed records reread during follow-up.

Direct EPUB review was targeted in the initial review. This follow-up identified no new disputed source proposition requiring another source reread. It is not an exhaustive fresh EPUB or graphical audit.
No modern Go behavior, external source or current runtime experiment is used to challenge BOOK-ERA advice.
All raw records contain operational guidance, so none is classified wholly as source_context. Historical explanatory claims can remain quarantined context inside retained records.

results.content_rationale: Present needs take precedence over speculative abstractions, with credible compatibility and later reassessment retained.
Future-reader clarity remains the objective, including names and representation rather than formatting alone.
Outer-variable assignment and a distinct temporary remain alternatives; intentional shadowing and scope analysis remain allowed.
Early returns and a left-aligned normal path reduce nesting while preserving behavior.
Cross-file init order remains unreliable, independently of package dependency order and deliberate side-effect imports.
Explicit dependency-aware initialization returns errors and state so callers retain failure policy and tests stay isolated.
Initialized mutable state is encapsulated instead of coupled through package globals.
Accessors need behavior or credible compatibility value; direct fields remain valid when accessors add nothing.
Getter/property and SetProperty naming retain the Go accessor convention.
Demonstrated shared behavior supports small reusable interfaces; Reader/Writer/sort examples are illustrative.
Injected behavior interfaces enable substitution and isolated tests without proving the external implementation works.
A restricted interface limits local capabilities, not mutations through other aliases.
Interfaces need demonstrated benefit; proven abstractions and single implementations remain legitimate exceptions.
Consumers define minimal local interfaces; established shared producer contracts remain valid.
Concrete results and useful interface inputs retain flexibility; error and established I/O results are exceptions.
Known types stay explicit; genuinely arbitrary-value APIs may use any.
Generic constraints retain comparability, underlying-type intent and the source-era method-parameter limitation.
Concrete type-related duplication justifies generic collections or shared algorithms with compile-time safety.
Method-only abstraction can use an interface directly; any generic design that harms clarity should be reconsidered.
Embedding requires intended API promotion, preserves the inner receiver and can eliminate interface forwarding boilerplate.
Evolving embedded types require ongoing API review; a team may avoid public embedding to avoid that burden.

Purposeful directories communicate roles, internal restricts imports, and the broader directory list is optional.

Nil slices support ordinary empty-slice operations; known size/elements and boundary contracts justify alternatives.
